॥ Om Dahara, the higher (subtle) principle ॥ 1/3/14 ॥

The nature of the base (adhara) from the moon to the sun has been stated to be Vishnu. And it is understood from the passage: “In this Brahma-city, the Dahara is the lotus-like dwelling; I am the Dahara; within this Dahara is the space (akasha)—what exists here?—both the earth and the sky are gathered within this space. Both fire and wind, and both the sun and the moon, lightning and the stars.” This space, however, is not Vishnu, as per the Vedic statement: “At its end is a subtle pore.” Therefore, he says: “Dahara, the higher (subtle) principle.”

From the higher qualities such as: “That Self, free from sin, free from old age, free from death, free from sorrow, free from hunger, free from thirst, with true desires and true resolve, is to be sought after and inquired into,” it is understood that Vishnu alone is the Dahara. For, it is Vishnu alone who possesses these qualities, as stated in the passages: “He who transcends hunger, thirst, sorrow, delusion, old age, and death,” and “He is this one who has risen above all sins.”

As stated in the Padma Purana: “The eternal, ever-liberated, one Hari, who is free from hunger and so on, is self-existent. Others cross over hunger and so on by His grace.”

And the absolute (nirapeksha) should be accepted over the relative (sappeksha). As stated in the Skanda Purana: “There is no one other than the imperishable Vishnu who is the ultimate reality of true desire. The state of having true desires in others arises from their desire for that (Vishnu).”
